concepts.label: Advanced TOUCH operation
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - genuinely new: couchbase.touch() resets a document's TTL/expiry without rewriting the document body or requiring a full round-trip write; not one of the get/upsert/replace/delete/insert operations eventing:advanced-keyspace-accessor's registry description enumerates, and round 8's Capella twin left this operation entirely unmodeled (empty concepts/relations)

relations.subject: server/8.0/eventing/eventing-handler-advancedTouchOp
relations.evidence: For more information about the Advanced TOUCH operation, see [Advanced TOUCH Operation](eventing-advanced-keyspace-accessors.md#advanced-touch-op).

notable_absence.finding: 'Does not require that you send the document back to the Data Service to update the TTL' is a documented contrast with the Basic/Advanced accessor write path (which does rewrite the whole document), but no existing predicate cleanly captures 'operation X, unlike sibling operations, does not require a full document write' - recorded here as a finding rather than forced into a relation. The availableSince claim above is a genuine addition over the Capella round: unlike the GET/INSERT/UPSERT/REPLACE/DELETE pages in this batch, which all cite a 3-tier 6.6.x/7.0+/7.1+ version ladder (implying those operations predate 7.0), this page cites only a single 'Version 7.6+' tier with no legacy fallback at all - the same single-tier signature this batch's advancedLookupInOp.md and advancedMutateInField.md/advancedMutateInArray.md use for their genuinely-new-in-7.6 sub-document operations, suggesting Advanced TOUCH is itself a 7.6-era addition to the Advanced Accessor family rather than a pre-7.0 operation, though the page doesn't state this outright - inferred from the version-comment pattern alone.
